context_documents.title: 2023-973 · Commercial structure and deletion of an unnecessary roller reduce development work
context_documents.body:
# 2023-973: Commercial structure and deletion of an unnecessary roller reduce development work

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The robot adapts a WCP GreyT elevator with two Falcons and a narrower configuration. The gripper evolves from side-grabbing concepts toward Everybot-style upper cone/lower cube contacts; an extra powered roller is removed after tests showed it was unnecessary.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly identifies commercial elevator parts as compatible with its manufacturing resources and describes the third roller as large and awkward without sufficient benefit. Swerve adoption was preceded by offseason work.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The useful reference is a tested simplification, not a claim that commercial hardware requires no engineering. Narrowing a standard structure changes bearing loads, stiffness and packaging. Removing a contact is justified when the remaining contacts retain acquisition and release tolerance across real piece conditions.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test the narrowed elevator for racking, validate pickup after collector deletion with worn pieces, and include offseason drive-training time in any comparison.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/89oDWctl8AI](https://youtu.be/89oDWctl8AI)

source_reviews.title: Greybots robot archive and MudSlide photograph
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the primary team season entry and visually inspected its full robot photograph.
source_reviews.facts: Team identifies MudSlide as its 2023 robot. The photo shows an inclined two-rail elevator, paired horizontal light-covered rollers, a wide low forward assembly and a pivot transmission adjacent to the head.
source_reviews.limitations: The archive has no robot-specific build narrative. One pose cannot establish motor identities, rigging sequence or chronology.

source_reviews.title: FIRST Updates Now, 973 Cube Rolling Strategy and Robot Overview
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the host's published interview summary. The linked video's captions could not be downloaded.
source_reviews.facts: The host identifies the cascade elevator, swerve and a wrist-enabled cube rolling strategy.
source_reviews.limitations: This is the host's summary, not a review of the team's spoken explanations. The historical first-swerve claim is contested in the thread.

source_reviews.title: Charged Up robot comparison and intake discussion
source_reviews.review_basis: Read thread and inspected both 973 images. The MudSlide image in post 6 duplicates the team archive view.
source_reviews.facts: A peer reports a wider cube intake at Champs. Another contributor describes 973's two-roller choice and aluminum wrist attachment as influences on 972.
source_reviews.limitations: Peer testimony, with a team archive photo supporting visible geometry. Image dates and exact part changes are not independently established.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: MudSlide pairs a swerve base and an inclined cascading elevator with a rotating roller head. The 2023 archive identifies the robot and supplies an unusually clear view of how the low head and large transverse assembly sit ahead of the rails. The host's contemporary account links wrist articulation to rolling cubes. That combination is the most defensible architectural finding. Team 973's own archive calls the 2023 machine MudSlide and uses WildFire for 2022, despite the name in FIRST's 2023 event record.
source_review.piece_flow: The team photo shows two closely spaced, transverse roller surfaces in the low wrist area. A second published view shows a cone held low and ahead of the mast. This establishes the location of cone retention in that pose, while the published interview summary establishes a cube rolling capability. The likely geometric division is that wrist pitch presents the roller contact while carriage movement provides height and fore-aft reach. Whether the wide lower assembly separately acquires and hands cubes to the head, or primarily assists ground contact in a particular pose, remains unresolved. Exact piece entry, transfer and release actions require spoken or visual sequence evidence.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The mast leans back from its lower mounting area. Accordingly, any straight travel up the visible rail direction shifts the carriage horizontally as well as vertically. Below the roller pair, the photograph shows a broader assembly occupying the low front space. Inference: these parts compete for envelope near a retracted mast, and the wide collector may create better cube approach tolerance only if the receiving pose clears the rail spacing and bumpers. Bench validation should include wrist sweep at intermediate lift heights and with a retained cone.

subsystems.name: Cascade elevator
subsystems.construction: Inclined, paired metal rails with nested members visible. The interviewer identifies cascade rigging in the written overview.
subsystems.operation: The elevator changes manipulator height and, because of the incline, changes horizontal offset as it travels.
subsystems.team_rationale: Robot-specific selection and manufacturing rationale could not be newly verified.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A narrow span can increase sensitivity to racking from an off-center piece. Measure diagonal movement and carriage error on abrupt reversal with the wrist extended.
subsystems.interfaces: The mast bolts into the chassis and the lower moving head occupies space directly in front of the rails.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect both sides for unequal stage travel and contact marks after lateral hits. Confirm harness clearance across moving stages.
subsystems.unknowns: Stage count, gearbox and motor specification, rigging details and exact commercial kit fit.

subsystems.name: Wrist and roller head
subsystems.construction: Paired cylindrical rollers and a side pivot transmission are visible. A peer identifies the wrist attachment as aluminum.
subsystems.operation: Wrist motion changes piece presentation. The host associates that motion with rolling cubes. A published photo shows a low carried cone.
subsystems.team_rationale: The peer reports that the two-roller and wrist attachment details influenced 972. Greybots' own rationale for contact count was not newly accessible.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Independent wrist orientation can compensate for the fixed mast angle. If rolling is used for release, surface friction and approach pitch can affect the result even at the same wrist setpoint.
subsystems.interfaces: Roller head attaches to the lift carriage. Low pitch brings it close to the bumper and wider front assembly.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check backlash, roller grip and symmetry. Test worn cube surfaces and cone flange deformation across the pickup and release envelopes.
subsystems.unknowns: Wrist ratio, roller drive and compliance, sensor confirmation and documented release poses.

subsystems.name: Wide front assembly and swerve
subsystems.construction: The team image shows a transverse lower assembly. A peer reports a wider cube intake for Champs. The host identifies swerve.
subsystems.operation: Swerve controls the field approach while the intake hardware sets the physical capture window.
subsystems.team_rationale: The wider cube intake is peer-reported. No primary design rationale or quantitative trade study was found.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Wider coverage can reduce centering demands while increasing leverage from side impact. Compare capture rates with actual approach error distributions.
subsystems.interfaces: Frame rail and bumper clearance govern how far the wider assembly can reach and retract.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect alignment after one-sided strikes and test for partial capture at the outer edges.
subsystems.unknowns: Module variant, collector drive, handoff sequence and as-built date.

revisions: A peer dates a wider cube intake to Champs. The photos corroborate the presence of a broad front assembly in one view. Prototype roller deletion and kit adaptation details from the corpus were not promoted to newly reviewed facts.
transferable_principles: Evaluate wrist pitch and mast angle jointly at contact and release. Judge a wider collector against measured alignment gains, swept clearance and service burden.
disconfirming_conditions: Wider ground coverage offers little if edge captures cannot be transferred consistently. Wrist-led cube rolling loses value if floor and piece variation make the final resting position unreliable.
remaining_gaps: Primary interview content, stage and motor details, direct versus assisted cube pickup sequence and dated verification of prototype changes.
